issue_context.body:

comments: It must be caused by repeated/duplicate calls to `httpcache.AddCacheControlToHeader`. That's not ideal, but luckily there is not side effect at the moment ....
Is there a reason to call `httpcache.AddCacheControlToHeader` 3 times? Looking on code, it seems it doesn't do anything different with each call
Of course no reason .... 😂 so that's not ideal.

review_comments:
Why not clean the incorrect calls?

This `Add` is somewhat done by purpose, to see how many calls to this function. And there may be other "Debug Headers" in the future, I just do not want to overwrite other values of the same header.

The three headers are added in the following order:
1. https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/4c59c8c7682da31410decba3bd868fde5116e073/modules/context/context.go#L756
2. https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/4c59c8c7682da31410decba3bd868fde5116e073/modules/httpcache/httpcache.go#L128
3. https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/4c59c8c7682da31410decba3bd868fde5116e073/modules/context/context.go#L391

How do you suggest to clean it?

Surprise .... actually there is already a conflict if I understand correctly: other `AddCacheControlToHeader` calls would drop the `"no-transform"` added before.

I think we need some new approaches for the cache header management.

<details>

To make the problem clear (instead of ignoring it) and remove duplicate header output and still remind future developers, I think a fix could be:

1. move the `Add("X-Gitea-Debug", "RUN_MODE="+setting.RunMode)` to `context.go` , only be called once.
2. use `Add("X-Gitea-Debug", "CacheControl=" + args ...)` in `AddCacheControlToHeader`.

Then, the future developers would see 4 X-Gitea-Debug headers like:

```
X-Gitea-Debug: RUN_MODE=dev
X-Gitea-Debug: CacheControl=0, no-transform
X-Gitea-Debug: CacheControl=300s
X-Gitea-Debug: CacheControl=180s
```

These headers will make developers think more about: hey, the calls to AddCacheControlToHeader overwrite others ...

Until there is a complete fix and the conflict would get fully fixed one day .....

</details>

See comment below, maybe it's as simple as making `SetCacheControlToHeader`  always overwrite cache control header.

Or, to be simple, take this PR (use `Set`), and add more comments about the duplicate calls of `AddCacheControlToHeader` problem in code.

And rename the `AddCacheControlToHeader` to `SetCacheControlToHeader`, then it's clear that by design it always overwrites cache control header values.
I pushed the rename, can you take over?
It looks clear to me, thank you ~~
